# apipbx_backup_settings (Resource)

How the server backs itself up: a singleton, needs a platform key. apipbxd makes the backups itself (a database dump, and the call recordings if included) at the time set, keeps the newest `keep` in `dir`, and can send each to another machine over SFTP. Only the attributes you set are sent. Destroying this resource leaves the settings as they are. Import with "backup".



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `dir` (String) The folder the backups go to (default /var/backups/apipbx). The service can write only under /var/backups/apipbx and /var/lib/apipbx: another folder must be allowed on the server first.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Make a backup every day (default true).
- `keep` (Number) How many backups stay on the server; the oldest are removed; 0 keeps all (default 14).
- `recordings` (Boolean) Include the call recordings, which are files and can be large (default true).
- `remote_enabled` (Boolean) Also copy each backup to another machine over SFTP.
- `remote_host` (String) The remote machine's host name or address.
- `remote_keep` (Number) How many backups stay on the remote machine; 0 keeps all (default 14).
- `remote_path` (String) The folder on the remote machine (made if it is missing).
- `remote_port` (Number) The remote SSH port (default 22).
- `remote_user` (String) The user on the remote machine.
- `time` (String) The time of day (server time, HH:MM) the daily backup is made at (default 03:00). One missed because the server was off is made when it is back.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `public_key` (String) The server's backup public key, made when the remote is enabled: add it to the remote user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.
